episodes.186441: Strong south winds developing ahead of an approaching low pressure system gusted briefly to storm force at the Grand Marais GLOS during the afternoon of 12th.
episodes.186942: A classic El Nino atmospheric setup, which included a robust subtropical jet stream aided by a slow-moving upper level disturbance that moved along the U.S. Mexico border and tapped into the jet, developed a surface coastal low/trough along and east of the Lower Texas coast beginning on November 9th/10th.  The situation continued through November 13th before the upper-level system moved east.  The steady, locally heavy rains were beneficial for most, with heavier pockets mainly producing ponding of water in urban areas. ||An area of heavier rain moved across the Rio Grande near Roma on the 12th, producing minor urban flooding.  Estimated rainfall totals for the entire event there were between 5 and more than 6 inches.
